--- lecture: "Outliers III" format: revealjs metadata-files: - _metadata.yml --- ## {{< meta lecture >}} {.large background-image="img/smooths.png" background-opacity="0.3" background-size="50%"} [DSCI 200]{.secondary} [{{< meta author >}}]{.secondary} Last modified -- 03 November 2026 $$ \DeclareMathOperator*{\argmin}{argmin} \DeclareMathOperator*{\argmax}{argmax} \DeclareMathOperator*{\minimize}{minimize} \DeclareMathOperator*{\maximize}{maximize} \DeclareMathOperator*{\find}{find} \DeclareMathOperator{\st}{subject\,\,to} \newcommand{\E}{E} \newcommand{\Expect}[1]{\E\left[ #1 \right]} \newcommand{\Var}[1]{\mathrm{Var}\left[ #1 \right]} \newcommand{\Cov}[2]{\mathrm{Cov}\left[#1,\ #2\right]} \newcommand{\given}{\ \vert\ } \newcommand{\X}{\mathbf{X}} \newcommand{\x}{\mathbf{x}} \newcommand{\y}{\mathbf{y}} \newcommand{\P}{\mathcal{P}} \newcommand{\R}{\mathbb{R}} \newcommand{\norm}[1]{\left\lVert #1 \right\rVert} \newcommand{\snorm}[1]{\lVert #1 \rVert} \newcommand{\tr}[1]{\mbox{tr}(#1)} \newcommand{\brt}{\widehat{\beta}^R_{s}} \newcommand{\brl}{\widehat{\beta}^R_{\lambda}} \newcommand{\bls}{\widehat{\beta}_{ols}} \newcommand{\blt}{\widehat{\beta}^L_{s}} \newcommand{\bll}{\widehat{\beta}^L_{\lambda}} \newcommand{\U}{\mathbf{U}} \newcommand{\D}{\mathbf{D}} \newcommand{\V}{\mathbf{V}} $$ ## Attribution
- Some examples and references are from [*Challenges of cellwise outliers*, by Raymaekers and Rousseeuw](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2452306224000078) - [*Robust Statistics*, by Maronna, Martin, Yohai, Salibian-Barrera](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9781119214656)
*In memory of my mentor and friend* Professor Ruben Zamar (1949-2023) who contributed greatly to Robust Statistics and beyond ...

## Review {.scrollable} - An **outlier** is an observation that deviates from the bulk of the data, an atypical observation. - We defined both casewise and cellwise outliers in a dataset, but focused on **univariate outliers**. - We examined by simulations three univariate estimators of location: the **mean**, the **median**, and the **M-estimators**. - We learned about the trade-off between robustness and efficiency. - We also learned about **masking** and robust outlier detection based on the **median** and **MAD**. ## From one variable to an entire dataset ::::: columns ::: {.column width="70%"} ![](img/overview.png) ::: ::: {.column width="30%"} Three core tasks: - **Estimating multivariate parameters** (e.g., location and covariance) - **Modeling relationships** (e.g., regression) - **Discovering structure** (e.g., unsupervised learning) ::: ::::: ## Goal for today 1. How do we detect outliers when we have several variables? 2. What happens when outliers affect **regression**? Can M-estimators help? 2. Identify different type of outliers: rowwise, cellwise and outlies in regression 3. Why do **cellwise** outliers need different tools? ## From one variable to many variables
### For one variable, we describe: - **center**: mean, median - **spread**: variance, SD, MAD ### For several variable, we describe: - **multivariate center**: the typical combination of values across variables. - **multivariate scatter**: how observations spread around the center, accounting for relationships between variables. ## ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: #### The center locates the data cloud, while scatter describes its shape and orientation. ## Robust multivariate estimators We want to estimate the center and spread of the data without being overly influenced by outliers. **Two possible strategies:** - 1. **M-estimators**: give less weight to observations that are far from the main cloud of data, reducing their influence on the estimated center and scatter. - 2. **Minimum covariace determinant (MCD)**: select the 50% of observations (or other) that form the most compact multivariate cloud. Estimate the center and spread using that group. ::: {.callout-tip title="Important"} Unlike **coordinate-wise** estimates and **pairwise** correlations, these methods consider all variables jointly to estimate the center and scatter. ::: ## ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} X <- glass_df[, c("V29", "V30", "V125", "V175", "V180")] # Classical estimates center_mean <- colMeans(X) center_median <- sapply(X, median) cov_classical <- cov(X) cor_classical <- cor(X) # Robust estimates (MCD) mcd <- robustbase::covMcd(X) center_MCD <- mcd$center cov_MCD <- mcd$cov cor_MCD <- mcd$cor # Multivariate MM-estimator mest <- covRob(as.matrix(X), type = "MM", corr = TRUE) center_MMest <- mest$center cov_MMest <- mest$cov cor_MMest <- mest$cor # Compare estimated centers round(rbind( Mean = center_mean, Median = center_median, MM = center_MMest, MCD = center_MCD ), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` V29 V30 V125 V175 V180 Mean 13.49 12.62 94.40 2013.37 511.22 Median 13.60 12.32 84.88 1754.15 466.60 MM 12.76 11.87 82.35 1729.24 450.51 MCD 12.46 11.63 79.33 1724.55 447.41 ``` ::: ::: ## ::: {.cell layout-ncol="3" layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-2.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-3.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: - **V125–V175**: the apparent positive relationship largely disappears with robust estimation. - **V175–V180**: The correlation remains very strong across all methods. ### Unusual observations can strongly affect estimated correlations when using classical estimators. # Rowwise outliers **How can we identify observations far from the main cloud?** ![](img/glass_row.png) ## Distance measure ### For univariate detection: a robust z-score $$z_i^{\text{rob}} = \frac{x_i-\text{median}}{\text{MAD}}$$ ### For multivariate detection: the Mahalanobis distance - We need a distance measure that accounts for the variability of each variable and the relationships between variables. ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} - Accounting for how the data vary, being far from the center does not necessarily mean being unusual. - Using robust estimates of center and scatter can help control masking. ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip title="Important"} An observation can be unusual **jointly** even if none of its individual values is extreme. ::: ## Detecting rowwise outliers - We can use the **MCD** or **MM-** estimates to calculate robust Mahalanobis distances (MD) of each data point. - The threshold is determined based on how this distance is expected to behave when the data follow a Normal distribution. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # MCD estimator mcd <- covMcd(X) md <- mahalanobis(X, mcd$center, mcd$cov) cutoff <- qchisq(0.975, ncol(X)) md_df <- data.frame( obs = seq_along(md), rob_MD = md, flagged = md > cutoff) ``` ::: ## ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(md_df, aes(x = obs, y = rob_MD)) + geom_point(aes(shape = flagged, color = flagged), size = 2) + scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) + scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "blue")) + geom_hline(yintercept = cutoff, linetype = "dashed") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: #### Data points (rows) with a squared MD exceeding the cutoff are flagged as rowwise outliers # Cellwise outliers **What if only a few values per observation are unusual in a row?** ![](img/glass_cell.png) ## ::: columns ::: {.column width="55%"}
### Cellwise outliers - In high-dimensional data, contamination often occurs cell by cell, not row by row. - Every row may contain at least one bad entry - Removing or downweighting entire rows with rowwise methods may discard useful information.
#### **Wrapping** extends the idea of robust estimation to individual cells. ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ![](img/Cell.png) ::: ::: ## Robust correlation by wrapping {.scrollable} In the spirit of Huber's estimation, wrapping have been proposed to compute robust correlations (fast):
::: columns ::: {.column width="55%"} - 1. robustly standardize each variable - 2. transform extreme values with a bounded function - 3. compute ordinary correlations on the transformed data ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ![](img/wrap.png) ::: ::: So we keep the speed and structure of classical correlation, but gain robustness.
::: {style="font-size: 13px; margin-top: -30px; color: grey;"} from Raymaekers, J., and Rousseeuw, P.J, (Technometrics 2021) ::: ## Detecting cellwise outliers
#### DDC: Detect Deviating Cells DDC combines robust correlation and regression to flag outlying cells. - **Robust correlations** identify related variables. - **Robust regressions** estimate relationships between pairs of variables. - These relationships are used to predict individual cell values. - Cells that deviate substantially from their predictions are flagged. - Missing and flagged values can be replaced by predicted values. #### DDC identifies unusual cells without discarding entire rows. ## Applying DDC to the Glass data
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # Run the fast DDC algorithm fastDDCglass <- DDC(X, list(fastDDC = TRUE, silent = TRUE)) # Create the cell map ggpfastDDC <- cellMap( R = fastDDCglass$stdResid, indcells = fastDDCglass$indcells, indrows = fastDDCglass$indrows, nrowsinblock = 5, mTitle = "", columnangle = 90 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` No rowblocklabels were given, so they are constructed automatically. ``` ::: ::: - `stdResid`: standardized differences between observed and predicted values. - `indcells`: cells flagged as unusual. - `indrows`: rows flagged as unusual. ## The cell map Let's visualize the suspicious entries in the Glass data. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-9-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=90%} ::: ::: **Yellow:** regular cells. **Red:** unusually high values. **Blue:** unusually low values. # Outliers in regression ## From multivariate outliers to regression ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} three_panel_reg ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-12-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ### Outliers can strongly influence regression estimates ## Least squares regression $$ \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{n} \ \sum_{i=1}^n (\underbrace{y_i - {\color{blue}{a}} - {\color{blue}{b}} x_i }_{\text{Residual}})^2 \end{equation*} $$ - LS finds ${\color{blue}{a}}$ and ${\color{blue}{b}}$ that minimizes the sum of the squared residuals. - Points with large residuals contribute heavily to the sum of squared residuals, pulling the LS fit toward them.




::: {style="font-size: 13px; margin-top: -30px; color: grey;"} Attribution: slides 23-25 are based on lecture notes from Prof. Salibian-Barrera ::: ## ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} #### Least squares: Minimizes the sum of squared residuals. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-14-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} #### Robust regression: Limits the influence of large residuals. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-15-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Robust regression (for rowwise outliers) #### **M-estimators** Replace square with a robust function $\rho(r)$ to limit the influence of outliers. > when $\sigma$ is unknown, we can use MM-estimation, which first estimates the scale robustly. $$ \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{n} \ \sum_{i=1}^n \rho \left(\frac{y_i - {\color{blue}{a}} - {\color{blue}{b}} x_i }{\sigma}\right) \end{equation*} $$ #### Least Trimmed Squares (LTS) Minimizes the sum of the 50% smallest squared residuals (or other proportion). ## ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(123) reg_ls <- lm(V175 ~ V125, data = dat) reg_mm <- lmrob(V175 ~ V125, data = dat) reg_lts <- ltsReg(V175 ~ V125, data = dat, alpha = 0.5) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-17-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 13px; margin-top: -30px; color: grey;"} Attribution: based on lecture notes from Prof. Salibian-Barrera ::: ## Outliers detection in regression ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # Add observation numbers dat <- dat |> mutate(id = row_number()) # Compute fitted values and standardized residuals diag_dat <- bind_rows( dat |> mutate( Method = "Least squares", fitted = fitted(reg_ls), std_resid = resid(reg_ls) / sigma(reg_ls) ), dat |> mutate( Method = "MM-estimation", fitted = fitted(reg_mm), std_resid = resid(reg_mm) / reg_mm$scale ), dat |> mutate( Method = "LTS", fitted = reg_lts$raw.coefficients[1] + reg_lts$raw.coefficients[2] * V125, std_resid = (V175 - fitted) / reg_lts$raw.scale ) ) |> mutate( Method = factor(Method, levels = c("Least squares", "MM-estimation", "LTS")), flag = abs(std_resid) > 2.5 ) # Select observations to label lab_dat <- diag_dat |> filter(flag) |> group_by(Method) |> slice_max(abs(std_resid), n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup() ``` ::: ## ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-19-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: #### Least squares can mask outliers because they pull the fitted line toward themselves, reducing their residuals. ## Regression outliers: residuals and leverage - **Vertical residual**: an observation far **vertically** from the fitted line. - **High-leverage observation** has an unusual value of the **predictor**, good or bad, depending on whether they follow the main data pattern. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} two_panel_reg ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](outliers-3_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-21-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ## Key Takeaways - In both univariate and multivariate cases, classical estimators can be sensitive to outliers. - Robust estimators reduce the influence of extreme observations, while aiming to maintain high efficiency under Normality. - **Rowwise contamination** - Methods such as M-estimators and MCD estimate robust multivariate center and scatter - These estimates can be used to compute robust Mahalanobis distances to detect outliers ## - **Cellwise contamination** - Methods such as DDC and wrapping detect corrupted cells - They rely on relationships among variables and are used to compute robust multivariate estimates and flag outliers - Robust methods improve both estimation and outlier detection - **Regression:** - M-estimators extend the robust-loss idea to residuals - LTS uses all data points to select a subset of points with smallest residuals - Outliers can be identified using residual plots from robust regression fits. - Large residuals and high leverage are different.

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
